stories.title: 4 cops including DSP martyred, 2 terrorists killed during exchange of fire in KP's Karak: police
summary: LAKKI MARWAT: Four policemen, including two officials, were martyred and two terrorists were killed during an exchange of fire in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa’s Karak district on Thursday, police said.

Police officers pay tribute to the martyred police personnel during funeral prayers in KP’s Karak on Oct 22. — photo courtesy KP police KP IGP Hameed paid tributes to the bravery, sense of duty, and professional commitment of the martyrs.

In September, two terrorists were killed in an intelligence-based operation in Lakki Marwat, and in August, a police constable was martyred and six officials were injured when an improvised explosive device was used to attack a police patrol van.

stories.title: Pakistan, Egypt, Saudi Arabia, Turkiye to meet European trio in Istanbul
summary: The R-4 group, which comprises Pakistan, Egypt, Saudi Arabia, and Turkiye, emerged in March and has been focusing on regional security and mediation efforts between the United States and Iran.

A Turkish diplomatic source told Reuters that the seven countries would meet in the R-4+E-3 format for the first time at Turkiye’s initiative as wars involving Iran, Yemen and Ukraine threaten shipping routes and regional security.

Fidan will also tell counterparts that Turkiye has been working to stop the war in Ukraine from spreading to the Black Sea, pointing to the regional security risks posed by the conflict, the source said.

stories.title: Direct flights between Pakistan and Maldives on the horizon as PM stresses connectivity
summary: Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif on Thursday announced that he had issued instructions for direct flights between Pakistan and the Maldives.

The premier was addressing the Pakistan-Maldives Business Forum, attended by visiting Maldivian President Dr Mohamed Muizzu, who arrived in Islamabad on Tuesday for a three-day trip at the invitation of PM Shehbaz.
The visit marks the first by a Maldivian president to Pakistan in 11 years, and comes as the two countries celebrate the 60th anniversary of their diplomatic relations, established in 1966.

stories.title: England's Brook hits record ODI double ton but Sri Lanka pull off epic chase in Rawalpindi clash
summary: England’s Harry Brook smashed the fastest double-century in One-Day International (ODI) history and became the first Englishman to score 200 in the format but Sri Lanka sealed a two-wicket win in their tri-series clash with one ball to spare in Rawalpindi on Thursday.
Brook’s scintillating performance ended with the final ball of England’s innings when he was caught by Sahan Arachchige off the bowling of Janith Liyanage.

The defeat leaves England bottom of the standings after losing both their matches, with Brook saying they need to win their next two games to reach the final in Lahore. “Unfortunately, it (the record) doesn’t matter now.

stories.title: China bets on manufactured water, and wants to sell it to the world
summary: China is emerging as a major supplier of water technology to parched countries across Asia, the Middle East and Africa, as shrinking natural supplies at home push Beijing to invest heavily in manufactured freshwater, industry experts say.

Peak water is the tipping point where flows from natural water sources reach a maximum and thereafter enter continual decline. “This will put almost half the GDP of 16 countries at risk, including China, CWR said.

Benjamin Horton, dean of the School of Energy and Environment at City University of Hong Kong, said China’s ability to develop water technology at scale could cut costs for other water-stressed countries.

stories.title: PM vows to bring back progress to KP, assails PTI's 'callousness' during its tenures
summary: Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif on Thursday vowed that the federal government, which now runs Khyber Pakhtunkhwa under governor’s rule, would make every effort possible to “bring back” progress to the province.

Emergency amid security challenges The Centre had imposed emergency and governor’s rule in KP on Oct 11, citing the PTI-led provincial government’s “deliberate disengagement” from the fight against terrorism.

In the meeting, the governor — who is now in charge of running the province — assured Naqvi he would enforce all policies of the federal government and work together with the security forces for peace and prosperity of the province.

stories.title: NBC to take up GM corn cases on Friday
summary: The National Biosafety Committee (NBC) meets on Friday to consider a range of biosafety applications, including long-pending cases related to genetically modified (GM) corn technologies, according to a statement issued on Thursday.
CropLife Pakistan, an industry body representing seed and crop-protection companies, said approval of the pending GM corn biosafety licences would mark a milestone for agricultural biotechnology.

CropLife Pakistan Executive Director Rasheed Ahmed said such a move could accelerate the adoption of advanced seed technologies, which he said would improve farm productivity, food security and the competitiveness of the sector.

stories.title: PSX falls below 164,000 on oil fears
summary: The Pakistan Stock Exchange's (PSX) benchmark KSE-100 index fell below the 164,000-point level on Thursday, shedding over 2,000 points as escalating geopolitical tensions and rising international oil prices heightened investor concerns over the economic outlook.

Topline's market review noted that the KSE-100 index witnessed a sharp sell-off, shedding 2,007 points (-1.21%), as escalating geopolitical tensions and rising international oil prices weighed on investor sentiment.
Pakistan Refinery was the volume leader with trading in 25.88 million shares, losing Rs4.76 to close at Rs95.12.

stories.title: Adviser calls for private control of energy sector
summary: Addressing the CEO Summit Islamabad 2026, organised by CEO Club Pakistan, he said high power costs undermined the competitiveness of domestic industries and stressed the need for affordable, reliable and sustainable energy supplies.

Referring to China's three decades of double-digit growth, the minister said Pakistan could draw lessons on promoting investment, expanding productive capacity and maintaining a long-term focus on economic transformation.
Muhammad Ali also thanked CEO Club Pakistan President and Founder Ijaz Nisar for convening the summit, saying such forums allowed meaningful discussion of economic challenges and growth prospects.

stories.title: Oil hits five-month high
summary: Brent futures rose $3.51, or 3.2%, to $112.33 a barrel at 1705 GMT, while US West Texas Intermediate crude rose $2.14, or 2.2%, to $99.29.
That drove Brent into technically overbought territory for a third time in a week and put it on track for the highest close since May 4.
Saudi Aramco told staff to evacuate its headquarters in Dhahran, as fighting between the world's largest crude exporter and Yemen's Houthis intensified.

stories.title: Growth to remain moderate at 4.2%
summary: The World Bank projected on Thursday a moderate 4.2% economic growth for Pakistan in the year before general elections in 2029 but urged the government to implement a plan to stay on course of macroeconomic stability in the election year.

The report discussed in depth Pakistan's current exchange rate policy, implying that such stability led to three macroeconomic crises in the recent past and adjustment was needed to arrest appreciation of the real effective exchange rate.
It underlined that Pakistan's current-to-medium-term growth rate was not enough to create jobs for 3.6 million people entering the market every year.

stories.title: Ambassador Sheikh calls for shift from ‘counterterrorism to IT’ in Pakistan-US ties
summary: Pakistan’s ambassador to the United States, Rizwan Saeed Sheikh, has called for a shift in bilateral engagement from counterterrorism to information technology, describing tech cooperation as a promising avenue for strengthening economic ties between the two countries.

Also Read: Ambassador Sheikh urges Pakistani-Americans to drive 'mutually rewarding' economic engagement The shift, participants noted, could help position Pakistani companies as higher-value partners in the global technology industry.
Concluding the event, Sheikh reiterated that Pakistan had arrived on the global technology stage and praised the participating companies as representatives of the country’s capabilities.

stories.title: ATC replaces state counsel in security breach case after Imaan, Hadi object to appointment
summary: RAWALPINDI: An anti-terrorism court (ATC) on Thursday cancelled the appointment of state counsel Taimoor Janjua in a security breach case against lawyers Imaan Zainab Mazari-Hazir and Hadi Ali Chattha, after the accused objected to his past conduct in another case.

Hearing the case on Thursday, Judge Sipra named Atif Mehmood as the replacement for Janjua, who was appointed as the state counsel just a day ago to conduct cross-examination of prosecution witnesses after the lawyer couple’s counsel failed to do so during proceedings.

During the proceedings, Imaan told the court that Janjua had previously been appointed as state counsel in another case involving her, referring to the controversial social media posts case in which they were sentenced in January.

stories.title: Punjab MPA Hina Parvez Butt defends deleted X post on alleged CCD encounter amid criticism
summary: Punjab lawmaker Hina Parvez Butt on Thursday defended herself after a social media post by her regarding an alleged encounter by Punjab’s Crime Control Department prompted outrage and criticism.
She also took exception to remarks by Punjab Information Minister Azma Bokhari, saying that she “respectfully disagreed”.
Referring to the remarks, Butt said: “None of my actions or words have ever harmed or embarrassed the Punjab chief minister or the government.

stories.title: Mir Raza murder case: Sindh minister says JIT to be formed as per judicial panel's suggestions
summary: Sindh Home Minister Ziaul Hassan Lanjar said on Thursday that a joint investigation team (JIT) would be formed as per the recommendations of the judicial commission formed to investigate the circumstances surrounding the murder of Mir Raza Ali.

A judicial commission, formed on the Sindh government’s directives after the family accused police of burying the facts, has declared that Ali’s death was a murder and pointed out lapses by the police during the probe.

Submitted to the government on Oct 15, the report by Sindh High Court judge Justice Omar Sial had recommended forming a JIT under the leadership of DIG Baloch to “balance the need for public accountability with preserving Sindh Police morale and reputation”.

stories.title: PHC bars arrest of inactive K-P deputy speaker, suspends eviction notice
summary: Advocate Yasir Khattak appeared on behalf of the petitioner, the inactive Deputy Speaker.
Opposing the petition, the Advocate General submitted that an emergency empowers the provincial government to reclaim official residences allotted to ministers, advisers and the Deputy Speaker.

The ruling provides immediate relief to the inactive Deputy Speaker and places the burden on the provincial authorities to justify the eviction drive in light of the statutory protections available to the holder of the office.

stories.title: DSP among 4 CTD, police personnel martyred in Karak attack
summary: Four police personnel, including a deputy superintendent of police (DSP) of the Counter-Terrorism Department (CTD), were martyred on Thursday in an exchange of fire with armed men in the Khurram Muhammad Zai area of Khyber-Pakhtunkhwa's Karak district.

Later, the funeral prayers for the police personnel were held with full state honours, which were attended by senior civil and military officials, police officers, family members of the martyrs and people from various walks of life.

The minister said K-P Police officers and personnel had made immense sacrifices in the fight against terrorism, adding that the nation remained indebted to the martyrs for their unparalleled sacrifices.

stories.title: Common ground
summary: IT appears that the PML-N, echoing the PPP’s recent offer, is also willing to re-engage with the opposition, at least on counterterrorism policy.
It is difficult to see how a credible counterterrorism strategy can be framed when the province on the front line of the fight has just been deprived of its elected government.
Yet the government seems consumed by the hubris of unchecked power, while the opposition, particularly the PTI, continues to act as if agitation alone can yield results.

stories.title: JI, govt to hold talks on Friday to work out plan for meeting between PM Shehbaz, Naeem
summary: Friday’s talks between the two sides’ negotiating committees will take place at Punjab House in Islamabad, where they will also work out a schedule for a proposed meeting between Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif and JI Emir Hafiz Naeemur Rehman, the party said.

According to the JI statement, Iqbal, who heads the government’s negotiating committee, informed Baloch that the meeting had initially been planned for Tuesday or Wednesday but was postponed because of the government’s “urgent engagements”.
On Sept 20, the party launched a protest march towards Islamabad, warning that if the government failed to abolish the petroleum levy, the protest could turn into one to oust the government.

stories.title: Govt cuts petrol by Rs1.60, increases diesel by 1.64 paisas for Oct 23
summary: Oil prices climbed about ​3% to a five-month high on Thursday after Houthi attacks in Saudi Arabia stoked concerns of further disruption to energy ‌supplies from the key exporting region.

"Reports ​of Middle East crude oil exports exceeding pre-conflict levels are more than countered by attacks on ships in the Strait of Hormuz and the ​Houthi strikes on Saudi Arabia and on its oil infrastructure," PVM Oil analyst Tamas Varga said.
Morgan Stanley analysts estimated that Middle East crude oil exports were around 17 million barrels per day last week.

stories.title: IMF says Middle East, North Africa and Pakistan GDP to contract 1.3pc in 2026
summary: The IMF said the region’s output was expected to contract by 1.3pc as a result of the war’s impact on energy production, shipping, tourism, trade and confidence.

The war’s impact had been substantial, but uneven, with oil-exporting economies directly affected by disruptions to energy production and shipping hit harder, and oil importers proving to be more resilient, the IMF said in its regional outlook released Thursday in Dubai.

Oil importers had proven more resilient, with domestic demand supported by remittances and tourism flows, favourable financial conditions, and prompt policy responses that safeguard consumers from higher commodity prices, the IMF said.

stories.title: NCCIA arrests Faisalabad man for alleged Saudi visa fraud via TikTok
summary: The National Cyber Crime Investigation Agency (NCCIA) said on Thursday it has arrested a suspect in Faisalabad for allegedly defrauding citizens through a TikTok account advertising visas for Saudi Arabia.

On Oct 10, NCCIA arrested 281 suspects, including 21 foreign nationals and 20 women, during operations against seven illegal call centres allegedly involved in financial fraud, online harassment and honey-trapping in Lahore.
In September, NCCIA, along with the Federal Investigation Agency, arrested six suspects involved in cyber fraud and financial scams, illegal money exchange and human trafficking across Punjab.

stories.title: 3 terrorists killed as security forces foil attack on construction camp in Gwadar: state media
summary: Security forces have killed three terrorists belonging to Fitna al-Hindustan while foiling an attempt to attack an unoccupied camp of a construction company in Balochistan's Gwadar, state-owned Radio Pakistan reported on Thursday, citing security sources.

Read: Armed men abduct 20 trainee police personnel travelling from Kalat to Nushki: officials In a separate attempted attack, an operation was under way against terrorists hiding in a local hotel near the Gwadar Highway, the report said.

In the aftermath of the attack, the Pakistan Army, Frontier Corps and Balochistan Police launched a joint operation, which remains underway, with forces intensifying action against terrorists across the province.

stories.title: Islamabad court sentences 2 men to 10 years for blackmailing 12-year-old girl with objectionable photos
summary: An Islamabad Additional District and Sessions Court on Thursday sentenced two men to 10 years in prison each and imposed a fine of Rs2 million on each after finding them guilty of blackmailing a 12-year-old girl and sharing her objectionable pictures.
The court sentenced both men to seven years in prison each and imposed a fine of Rs1 million on each under Section 22 of the Prevention of Electronic Crimes Act, 2016 (PECA).

Read: AI to be used in online child abuse probes Under Section 24 of PECA, both convicts were sentenced to an additional three years in prison each and fined Rs1 million each, bringing their total prison term to 10 years each and the fine to Rs2 million each.

stories.title: Targeted by Trump, International Criminal Court wins top EU rights prize
summary: This month, the United States announced sanctions against the ICC aimed at crippling the day-to-day operations of the court, which tries individuals for war crimes, crimes against humanity and genocide.

The win comes after ex-ICC judge Navi Pillay, who also served as UN rights chief, was awarded the Nobel Peace Prize this month — a choice Trump slammed as “disgraceful”, arguing the award should have gone to him.
The ICC was among three finalists this year, alongside Tanzania opposition leader Tundu Lissu and twin sisters Taraneh and Romina Rahimi, representing those prosecuted by the Iranian government.

stories.title: Tally hits 95 as two more monkeypox cases reported in Sindh
summary: Experts said mpox is a viral disease that can spread through close physical or skin-to-skin contact with an infected person, as well as contact with lesions, bodily fluids or contaminated objects.
People developing symptoms have been advised to avoid close contact with others and seek immediate medical evaluation and diagnostic testing.
People experiencing fever, swollen lymph nodes or unusual skin rashes and blisters should seek immediate medical attention.

stories.title: Earthquake of magnitude 7 strikes China's Tibet
summary: A magnitude 7.0 earthquake struck China's southwestern region of Tibet at around 10:33pm (1433 GMT) on Thursday, ​the China Earthquake Networks Centre (CENC) said.
The quake was clearly felt in the local area, CENC said.
A string of smaller tremors of around magnitude ​3 and 4 have been recorded in surrounding ​regions following ⁠the magnitude 7 quake, CENC data showed.

stories.title: President Zardari departs for Germany on 3-day visit to discuss bilateral ties
summary: President Asif Ali Zardari departed for Germany on Thursday on a three-day visit to discuss bilateral ties as the two countries are set to mark the 75th anniversary of their diplomatic relations.
In a statement issued earlier, the Foreign Office (FO) said the president’s visit, scheduled for Oct 22-24, is “part of high-level exchanges between Pakistan and Germany”.

During his visit, President Zardari will hold meetings with his German counterpart Frank-Walter Steinmeier, as well as senior leadership and business leaders, with a “particular focus оп economic and trade cooperation”, FO said.

stories.title: Pakistan, EU agree to strengthen counterterrorism cooperation at multilateral forums
summary: Pakistan and the European Union (EU) have agreed to strengthen cooperation at multilateral forums, including the United Nations, to advance a coherent counterterrorism approach, according to a statement issued by the Foreign Office (FO) on Thursday.
The dialogue comes as Pakistan’s counterterrorism challenge enters a new and more complex phase, with terrorist groups evolving their methods of financing and recruitment.

On Tuesday, an international seminar on Pakistan’s evolving counterterrorism landscape, organised by the Institute of Strategic Studies Islamabad, highlighted the changing methods of terrorist groups, including their financing and recruitment.

stories.title: Pakistan, Maldives move to establish direct air links
summary: Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif on Thursday said he had directed the Ministry of Aviation to explore ways to establish direct flights between Pakistan and the Maldives, as the two countries agreed to strengthen air connectivity and expand bilateral trade.

Highlighting the importance of connectivity, PM Shehbaz said there were currently no direct flights between Pakistan and the Maldives, making the establishment of an air link essential to closer bilateral relations. “Connectivity is very important.

Emphasising the importance of maritime connectivity, the prime minister said the two countries would find it difficult to achieve their trade targets efficiently without a direct shipping schedule between Karachi or Gwadar and Malé.

stories.title: Nvidia boss criticises 'cheap' AI doomsday warnings
summary: While such statements generate "headlines", they were "made up" and "cheap", added Huang, whose visit to Berlin is the final stop of a European tour.
Read: DeepSeek wrapping up $15b fundraising to fuel AI race, sources say Huang, however, is firmly in the opposing camp, and has advocated for development of the technology to move full steam ahead.
During Huang's European tour, Nvidia pledged nearly $10 billion in investments in the continent's technology sector and urged Europe, which is lagging behind in the AI race, to move faster.

stories.title: France reports first human case of livestock virus Shamonda after patient dies
summary: France on Thursday reported the first ‌human case of the Shamonda virus, usually found in livestock, in a patient who later died, with authorities adding there was no risk to the general population at this stage.

Virus spreading in animals in Europe Shamonda is transmitted by biting midges and most commonly found in cattle, though it has also been found in horses, alpacas, sheep and goats, according to the World Organisation for ​Animal Health (WOAH).
The virus has several effects on ⁠animals, with affected cattle ​showing diarrhoea, weakness, loss of appetite and, less often, ​fever, French animal health authorities said.

stories.title: Faster reforms could triple Pakistan’s incomes by 2050, says World Bank
summary: The report says that following progress on macroeconomic stabilisation, Pakistan has an opportunity to achieve faster and sustained economic growth and create more jobs.
The report finds that higher growth is possible if Pakistan follows the path taken by other successful countries in pursuing ambitious economic reforms.
The report outlines an ambitious set of reforms that could enable Pakistan to attain by 2050 the per capita income levels of countries currently at the upper-middle-income threshold.

stories.title: Millions of hacking attempts as companies, governments rush to patch PHP flaws
summary: Global firms and governments rushed on Thursday ​to patch critical flaws in the PHP programming language that underpins much of the internet, as a cloud firm reported millions of hacking attempts after vulnerabilities were disclosed.
As companies and governments deployed patches and suspended websites as a precaution, hacking attempts surged into the millions, according to cloud services firm Cloudflare.
Some ​fixes may take weeks to implement Several Asian governments ordered cybersecurity inspections related to the PHP vulnerabilities on Thursday.

stories.title: New Delhi steps up air pollution controls ahead of winter
summary: India began annual measures on Thursday to tackle toxic air pollution in New Delhi, a megacity of 30 million people regularly ranked among the world’s most polluted capitals.

In previous years, such measures have failed to curb pollution, which peaks from November to January, when levels of cancer-causing PM 2.5 microparticles often hit more than 300 micrograms per cubic metre, 20 times the World Health Organisation’s recommended daily maximum.
Last year, pollution levels peaked at 846 micrograms per cubic metre, 56 times the WHO limit.

stories.title: LHC summons Punjab home secretary, Kot Lakhpat jail superintendent in plea seeking release of Imran’s sisters
summary: LAHORE: The Lahore High Court (LHC) on Thursday summoned the Punjab home secretary and the superintendent of Kot Lakhpat jail in connection with a petition seeking the release of former prime minister Imran Khan’s three sisters.
It stated that Imran’s sisters remained at Lahore’s Kot Lakhpat jail despite the lapse of the 30-day period of their detention.
In Wednesday’s petition, Shahrez contended that the detention period had expired, but the three sisters remained in custody.

stories.title: Karachi judicial magistrate rejects bail plea of anchorperson Iqrarul Hassan
summary: KARACHI: A local court on Thursday rejected TV anchorperson Iqrarul Hassan’s bail plea in a cybercrime case pertaining to the alleged dissemination of anti-state content.
Earlier this week, Hassan was sent to prison on judicial remand after the NCCIA sought an extension of his physical remand by another eight days.
The court also issued notices to the NCCIA on a bail application filed by Hassan’s defence counsel, Barrister Mian Ali Ashfaq, and fixed the matter for hearing on Oct 21.

stories.title: LHC issues notices to foreign secretary in contempt cases over detention of PTI-linked Pakistanis in UAE
summary: On September 14, the LHC had directed the foreign secretary to process and decide within 15 days representations concerning the detention of two citizens — Syed Salman Raza Zaidi and Muhammad Junaid Jahangir.

The counsel for the petitioners submitted that despite representations having been filed regarding the detention of both citizens before the foreign secretary, the representations had not been processed.

Both petitioners had asked the court to direct that legal and consular assistance be provided to Zaidi and Jahangir, that their judicial records be obtained and that diplomatic-level steps be taken toward their return to Pakistan.
